questions.question: What makes a model layer a sparse mixture of experts?
options: A router activates only a bounded subset of expert networks for each token.
Every token executes every expert and averages all outputs.
The service chooses one database for the whole request.
Image tokens bypass the model and are stored in a cache.
questions.explanation: Sparse MoE uses conditional computation: the router selects one or a few expert paths per token rather than executing the full expert pool.

questions.question: Why should a multimodal routing report preserve modality slices?
options: Global balance can hide poor routes or overflow concentrated in one modality.
Modality labels make expert capacity unlimited.
Every expert must be manually assigned to exactly one modality.
Text and image token counts are always equal.
questions.explanation: Image, text, and joint tokens can differ in count and routing behavior, so an aggregate expert histogram can hide modality-specific harm.

questions.question: A routing group has 800 tokens, top-2 routing, 8 routed experts, and a capacity factor of 1.25. What is the planning capacity per expert before implementation-specific rounding?
options: 250 assignments
125 assignments
800 assignments
2,000 assignments
questions.explanation: Capacity is 800 x 2 x 1.25 / 8 = 250 assignments per expert. The formula counts top-k assignments, not requests.

questions.question: What does shared-plus-routed execution imply for active work?
options: Every token executes the shared expert and its selected routed expert path.
The shared expert runs only after an HTTP request fails.
No routed expert weights need to be stored.
The router no longer needs capacity controls.
questions.explanation: A shared expert is a normal active compute path for every token in this architecture, while routed experts add conditional capacity.

questions.question: What is the main risk of silently dropping an overflowed expert assignment?
options: The residual path may continue while the token loses specialized processing, changing quality without a request error.
The model always returns an HTTP 500 before decoding.
All expert weights are deleted from memory.
The router automatically retrains itself during inference.
questions.explanation: Internal token dropping can preserve service availability while removing conditional computation, so quality can degrade silently and unevenly.

questions.question: Which evidence is strongest for promoting a new router and overflow policy?
options: Task and grounding quality by modality and route, plus overflow, communication, tail latency, and cost under realistic pressure.
Only a lower average auxiliary routing loss on the training batch.
Only a uniform expert histogram with no task evaluation.
Only the total parameter count in the checkpoint.
questions.explanation: Routing is part of both model behavior and serving behavior, so promotion requires joint quality, capacity, communication, latency, and cost evidence.
